Frontend Application¶

Overview¶

The frontend provides a web-based interface for the BMW Dealer Inventory Recommendation system.

It allows users to select a dealer and BMW model and view the inventory recommendation generated by the backend.

The frontend is implemented using React.

Frontend Architecture¶

The frontend communicates with the FastAPI backend through HTTP requests.

The overall flow is:

User
 |
 v
React UI
 |
 | Select Dealer + Model
 v
FastAPI
 |
 | POST /recommend
 v
Recommendation Engine
 |
 v
JSON Response
 |
 v
React UI
 |
 v
Recommendation Display

Technology¶

The frontend uses:

  • React

  • JavaScript

  • HTML

  • CSS

  • React Select

React¶

React is used to build the user interface using reusable components.

JavaScript¶

JavaScript handles frontend interaction and communication with the backend API.

React Select¶

React Select is used for dealer and BMW model selection.

It provides searchable dropdown controls for selecting the required inputs.

User Workflow¶

The typical user workflow is:

  1. Open the inventory recommendation application.

  2. Select a dealer.

  3. Select a BMW model.

  4. Submit the recommendation request.

  5. Wait for the backend response.

  6. View the predicted demand and recommended quantity.

  7. Read the generated explanation.

Dealer Selection¶

The frontend retrieves the available dealer IDs from the FastAPI /options endpoint.

The returned dealer list is displayed as a selectable dropdown.

Example:

Dealer
[ D001 v ]

Model Selection¶

The frontend also retrieves available BMW models from the /options endpoint.

Example:

BMW Model
[ 2 Series v ]

Recommendation Request¶

After the user selects a dealer and model, the frontend sends a POST request to the backend.

Example request:

{
    "dealer_id": "D001",
    "model": "2 Series"
}

The request is sent to:

POST /recommend

Recommendation Display¶

The frontend displays the information returned by the recommendation engine.

Important information includes:

  • Dealer

  • BMW model

  • Recommended quantity

  • Predicted next-month demand

  • Current inventory

  • Target inventory

  • Days of inventory

  • Sales trend

  • Recommendation reason

Frontend and Backend Integration¶

The frontend and backend run as separate applications during local development.

The typical development setup is:

React
localhost:5173
     |
     | HTTP
     v
FastAPI
localhost:8000
     |
     v
Recommendation Engine

CORS¶

Because the React frontend and FastAPI backend run on different local ports, Cross-Origin Resource Sharing is configured in the backend.

The development frontend origins include:

http://localhost:5173
http://127.0.0.1:5173

This allows browser requests from the React application to reach the FastAPI service.

Frontend Error Handling¶

The frontend should handle common request states such as:

  • Loading

  • Successful response

  • Invalid input

  • Backend errors

  • Network failures

This prevents the user from seeing an unclear or incomplete application state when the backend is unavailable.

Development¶

The React frontend can be started using the project’s configured npm development command.

The development server uses port:

5173

Frontend Project Structure¶

The frontend is maintained separately from the Python backend.

A typical structure is:

frontend/
|
+-- src/
|    |
|    +-- components/
|    +-- App.jsx
|    +-- main.jsx
|
+-- package.json
+-- Dockerfile
+-- .dockerignore

Container Support¶

The frontend includes a Dockerfile for containerized development.

The Docker image uses Node.js and exposes port 5173.

The container starts the React development server using:

npm run dev -- --host

Docker support is kept separate from the Python backend so that the frontend and backend can be developed independently.

Design Goals¶

The frontend is designed to provide:

  • Simple dealer and model selection

  • Clear recommendation output

  • Easy-to-read inventory information

  • Human-readable recommendation reasoning

  • Separation between user interface and backend processing

Future Improvements¶

Potential frontend improvements include:

  • Production build optimization

  • Responsive design improvements

  • Authentication

  • Role-based access

  • Recommendation history

  • Dealer-level dashboards

  • Inventory trend charts

  • Model comparison

  • Exporting recommendations

  • Integration with production backend services
